prerequisite_rule: Needs the Unstable Unicorns base game.
what_it_adds: Instant cards that are not Neigh cards, flexible choose-an-effect cards, a new cast of characters and adventure-themed art, in a 54-card pack.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.37 from 276 ratings, second to Nightmares among full packs. It adds non-Neigh Instants and choose-your-effect cards instead of more of the same Neigh play.
notes: BGG avg 7.37 over 276 ratings read 2026-10-15. Card count 54 from BGG publisher description; TeeTurtle product page lists $15.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Unstable Unicorns base game.
what_it_adds: Horror-themed Character, Magic, Upgrade, Instant and Nightmare Downgrade cards plus Baby Unicorns, 54 cards in total.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.43 from 133 ratings, the top score among full 54-card packs. It adds horror-themed cards, including Nightmare Downgrades, with no new rules to teach.
notes: BGG avg 7.43 over 133 ratings read 2026-10-15. Card mix (12 Basic, 11 Magical Unicorn, 10 Magic, 4 Downgrade, 9 Upgrade, 4 Instant, 3 Baby, 1 reference) is from the BGG description.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Unstable Unicorns base game.
what_it_adds: A 54-card pack of battle-hardened unicorns and magic cards that follow the base game structure.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.13 from 546 ratings, above Dragons (7.0) and Rainbow Apocalypse (6.92). It is a straight card-variety add with no new rules.
notes: BGG avg 7.13 over 546 ratings read 2026-10-15.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Unstable Unicorns base game.
what_it_adds: Dragon-themed Upgrade, Downgrade and Magic cards plus new Unicorns, 54 cards in total.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.0 from 877 ratings, a middling score. Buy it for the dragon theme; the Kickstarter version has 27 fewer cards, so check which copy you get.
notes: BGG avg 7.0 over 877 ratings read 2026-10-15. A BGG poster reports the Kickstarter Dragons pack has 27 fewer cards than the retail 54-card version.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Unstable Unicorns base game. It also works with the NSFW edition.
what_it_adds: Holiday-themed Character, Magic, Upgrade and Downgrade cards in a 36-card pack.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.46 from 130 ratings, but only 36 cards and holiday-only theme. Worth it only if you play at Christmas.
notes: BGG avg 7.46 over 130 ratings read 2026-10-15. The BGG description and TeeTurtle page both say 36 cards; TeeTurtle price $12.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Unstable Unicorns base game.
what_it_adds: Two 27-card sets in one pack: Rainbow Sprinkles (cute cards) and Apocalypse (destructive cards), 54 cards in total.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 6.92 from 785 ratings. BGG posters say the Apocalypse cards stretch playtime too much, and TeeTurtle listed it unavailable on 2026-10-15.
notes: BGG avg 6.92 over 785 ratings read 2026-10-15. TeeTurtle product JSON showed no variant available on 2026-10-15, so the link is for reference and stock.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Unstable Unicorns base game. It is rated for adult groups.
what_it_adds: 54 adult-themed cards that you shuffle into the base deck, or two packs together for a full adult game.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 6.74 from 842 ratings, lowest of the packs. A BGG poster still calls it the best one to start with, but it is an adults-only deck.
notes: The BGG forum calls the NSFW pack the Uncut expansion pack. TeeTurtle now sells a 114-card NSFW base game at $20 (ages 21+) rather than the 54-card pack, and its Christmas page says that pack works with the NSFW game; price and link are for that current product.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Exploding Kittens base game. Language versions must match.
what_it_adds: 15 new cards including the Streaking Kitten, which lets a player hold an Exploding Kitten in hand without exploding, plus cards to mess with the deck and other players.
what_it_fixes: A BGG poster says the base game feels like going through the motions without it; the new cards add choices that make play less random.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.15 from 2,672 ratings. In a BGG thread, two players pick it as the one expansion to buy and one calls the base game close to unplayable without it.
notes: Publisher shop showed $3.99 against a $6.99 compare-at price on 2026-10-15. The shop warns non-English versions are not compatible with English Exploding Kittens sets. BGG 7.15 over 2672 ratings read 2026-10-15.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Exploding Kittens base game. Language versions must match.
what_it_adds: 20 new cards including a pair of Barking Kitten cards that work like a game of chicken, plus a Cat Crown that lets you hold a secret stash of cards.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 6.8 from 1,276 ratings. A BGG player who owns all three ranked it second behind Streaking Kittens and ahead of Imploding Kittens.
notes: BGG 6.8 over 1276 ratings read 2026-10-15. The ordering quote is one BGG poster, backed by another saying Streaking is a must.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Exploding Kittens base game. Language versions must match.
what_it_adds: 20 new cards, a face-up Imploding Kitten that cannot be defused, a Cone of Shame turn marker, and support for up to 6 players.
what_it_fixes: Raises the player cap from 5 to 6.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 6.98 from 5,641 ratings. Posters split: one finds the draw-from-bottom and Alter the Future cards game-changing, another plays without the Imploding card because it is easy to spot.
notes: BGG 6.98 over 5641 ratings read 2026-10-15. Buy it first only if you need the sixth seat.

prerequisite_rule: Works alone or can be mixed into Exploding Kittens.
what_it_adds: A zombie deck where dead players keep their hand, play cards to torment the living and can come back from the dead. BGG lists a 22-card expansion version.
what_it_fixes: Eliminated players stay in the game instead of watching.
verdict_reason: BGG rates the 22-card expansion version only 6.33 from 28 ratings, so little data. BGG players say it mixes into the base game or runs alone and pairs well with Recipes for Disaster.
notes: The publisher shop sells the full standalone Zombie Kittens set at $19.99, not the 22-card expansion BGG lists; a BGG poster confirms both versions exist. Ranking name Zombie Kittens Expansion kept as Zombie Kittens. Rated on only 28 BGG ratings.

prerequisite_rule: Needs The Resistance base game.
what_it_adds: Three modules: Assassin (the Avalon roles rethemed for The Resistance), Defector (spies who switch sides) and Trapper (the leader isolates one team member).
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.64 from 884 ratings, the highest of the three expansions. BGG threads call the Assassin roles must-have or strongly recommended and the first module to add.
notes: BGG 7.64 over 884 ratings read 2026-10-15. Publisher page lists MSRP $19.99. One BGG poster says the purest experience is 5-player vanilla, so it is strongly recommended rather than mandatory.

prerequisite_rule: Needs The Resistance base game.
what_it_adds: The Plot Cards module from the second edition plus the Rogue and Sergeant modules, a full set of replacement Character and Mission cards and new tracking tokens.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.45 from 201 ratings. Posters split: some always play with plot cards and find the Resistance disadvantaged without them, another finds them redundant once roles are in.
notes: BGG 7.45 over 201 ratings read 2026-10-15. Publisher page lists MSRP $19.99.

prerequisite_rule: Needs The Resistance base game.
what_it_adds: Three modules: Hunter (both teams must find a specific opposing leader), Reverser (flips mission results) and Inquisitor (look at another player allegiance).
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.23 from 498 ratings, below Hidden Agenda. A BGG poster says the Hunter module looks more complex and the Inquisitor can be simulated with base cards.
notes: BGG 7.23 over 498 ratings read 2026-10-15. Publisher page lists MSRP $24.99.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Coup base game.
what_it_adds: 15 additional character cards and faction rules: each player is Loyalist or Reformist, can target only the other faction, and can convert by paying the Almshouse.
what_it_fixes: Lets Coup play well with up to 10 players and adds early tension for four or more.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.25 from 6,153 ratings. It is the main expansion; a BGG thread calls base Coup plus Reformation the complete game, and it extends play from 6 to 10 players.
notes: BGG 7.25 over 6153 ratings read 2026-10-15. Publisher page lists MSRP $19.99 and the Amazon listing is the 2nd edition (Loyalist/Reformist). The first edition used Catholic and Reformist; BGG says the expansion works with the original Coup. Coup base MSRP not shown on the publisher page.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Here to Slay base game.
what_it_adds: Berserker and Necromancer classes: new party leaders, heroes and monsters in 31 standard cards, 2 oversized Party Leaders and 2 oversized Monsters.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.51 from 760 ratings, slightly above Warriors & Druids. It adds two new classes with leaders, heroes and monsters.
notes: BGG 7.51 over 760 ratings read 2026-10-15. A BGG poster says rules do not change when you add more than one class expansion. Once mixed into the base deck it is hard to separate again, per a BGG poster.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Here to Slay base game.
what_it_adds: Warrior and Druid classes: new party leaders, heroes and monsters in 31 standard cards, 2 oversized Party Leaders and 2 oversized Monsters.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.44 from 1,111 ratings, the most rated expansion. A BGG poster likes the new leaders and monsters but says some class abilities rarely come up.
notes: BGG 7.44 over 1111 ratings read 2026-10-15. BGG posters also say expansions lengthen the game and are hard to separate once mixed in.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Here to Slay base game.
what_it_adds: New effects and mechanics plus a new win condition: claim Banners by building your party, with 32 standard cards, 13 oversized cards and 20 tokens.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.46, but from only 42 ratings. It adds a new way to win and banner stealing, so it changes the game more than a new-class pack.
notes: BGG 8.46 over 42 ratings read 2026-10-15, so the rating is a small sample. The ranking list called it Banner Quest; the BGG thread title is Banners Quest.

expansion_name: Here to Slay: Here to Sleigh
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Here to Slay base game. It is for 2 to 4 players.
what_it_adds: Holiday artwork, new card types and a new win condition: complete checklist objectives and gather Gift cards.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 6.84 from 175 ratings, the lowest of the Here to Slay expansions. It is seasonal and limited to 2-4 players.
notes: BGG 6.84 over 175 ratings read 2026-10-15. Product has 30 standard cards, 22 Gift cards, 4 Holiday Overlay cards, 4 Checklist cards and 10 clips per the publisher page.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Here to Slay base game.
what_it_adds: 13 oversized Monster cards to add to the monster deck. It was a Kickstarter exclusive.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.55 from 204 ratings, but it was Kickstarter-exclusive. BGG posters say you can only get it on the secondary market or via a later Kickstarter pledge manager.
notes: No publisher shop listing found on teeturtle.com on 2026-10-15; BGG reference link only. Availability comes from BGG forum posts, not from the publisher.

expansion_name: Here to Slay: Dragon Sorcerer Expansion
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Here to Slay base game.
what_it_adds: A new class of Heroes, a Dragon Sorcerer Party Leader, a new Monster card and extra Item, Magic, Modifier and Challenge cards. It was a Kickstarter exclusive.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.46 from 233 ratings, but it was Kickstarter-exclusive. BGG posters say it is secondary-market only, or sometimes offered through a pledge manager.
notes: No publisher shop listing found on teeturtle.com on 2026-10-15; BGG reference link only. The publisher says the Sorcerers are being reissued with new art in Sorcerers & Squires (BGG year 2027, release unverified, so not ranked).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Here to Slay base game. Release is not confirmed.
what_it_adds: Reissues the Sorcerer class with new art and adds Squires, a support class whose Hero effects need no dice roll, per the publisher text on BGG.
notes: Not ranked: announced 2026-04-03 as a crowdfunding preorder, BGG lists year 2027 with one rating and no reviews, and no retail listing exists, so release and contents are unverified.

expansion_name: Arkham Horror (Third Edition): Dead of Night
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Arkham Horror Third Edition base game.
what_it_adds: Two new scenarios, new investigators including Roland Banks, and eight more encounter cards per neighbourhood, doubling the base encounter decks.
what_it_fixes: Fixes repeating encounters: the core box has only eight encounter cards per neighbourhood.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.29 from 1,446 ratings. BGG posters say buy it first: it doubles each neighbourhood encounter deck and is the cheapest by MSRP, though it has the fewest scenarios.
notes: BGG 8.29 over 1446 ratings read 2026-10-15. Scenario count (2) and encounter-card counts come from BGG forum posters, not from the publisher. No Amazon listing found by search on 2026-10-15; the FFG page only lists rules for it.

expansion_name: Arkham Horror (Third Edition): Under Dark Waves
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Arkham Horror Third Edition base game.
what_it_adds: Four new scenarios, eight new investigators and special locations, with minor new mechanics.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.42 from 1,036 ratings. BGG posters call its scenarios easier and more numerous (four) than Secrets of the Order, but say it feels less polished.
notes: BGG 8.42 over 1036 ratings read 2026-10-15. Scenario count and difficulty are BGG poster claims; a BGG thread also asks whether it fits in the core box.

expansion_name: Arkham Horror (Third Edition): Secrets of the Order
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Arkham Horror Third Edition base game.
what_it_adds: Three scenarios with interesting layouts, hidden monsters and special locations, plus four new investigators including Agatha and Winifred.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.46 from 690 ratings, the highest of the three. A BGG poster ranks it the best expansion, but others warn two of its scenarios are among the hardest in the game.
notes: BGG 8.46 over 690 ratings read 2026-10-15. No Amazon listing found by search on 2026-10-15, so BGG reference link only. Investigator counts come from BGG posters.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Blood Rage base game.
what_it_adds: Mystic units (neither warrior nor monster, strength 2, invade at no Rage cost) unlocked by new Clan Upgrades that each give your Mystics a special ability.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.89 from 3,272 ratings. Several BGG posters add it to every game, though others say it adds little.
notes: BGG 7.89 over 3272 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3155099 (2023): some posters always play with Mystics, one says they do not add much. Each clan may recruit at most 2 Mystics per the BGG description.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Blood Rage base game and a group of five.
what_it_adds: The Ram clan (8 warriors, leader, ship, clan sheet) and 24 Gods Gifts cards for five-player games; no province is destroyed before the game starts.
what_it_fixes: Lets a fifth person play; the core box only seats four.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.07 from 3,381 ratings. Only worth buying if you will play with five; one BGG poster says five is their favourite count, another calls it crowded and chaotic.
notes: BGG 8.07 over 3381 ratings read 2026-10-15. Components and the five-player rule come from the BGG publisher description. No Amazon listing found by search on 2026-10-15, so BGG reference link only.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Blood Rage base game.
what_it_adds: Two random gods per game sit in provinces and change that province rules; each pillage moves a god, and gods are redrawn each Age.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.64 from 3,060 ratings. BGG posters are split: one always plays with it, others skip it or save it for experienced groups.
notes: BGG 7.64 over 3060 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3155099 (2023) opinions are mixed, as quoted in the reason.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Caverna: The Cave Farmers base game.
what_it_adds: Eight species or race packs (elves, dark elves, trolls and more) that each player can play instead of dwarves, each with four unique rooms that replace base-game rooms.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.22 from 1,671 ratings, the best of the large expansions. One BGG poster says it adds interesting twists while the game stays fun.
notes: BGG 8.22 over 1671 ratings read 2026-10-15. Began as a BGG fan project that Lookout adopted. Thread 3025686 (2023) says it added twists without making the game miserable. A 2019 thread notes a reprint after first-edition misprints.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Caverna: The Cave Farmers base game.
what_it_adds: Orc raiders you fight with axes, keep out with traps or weaken with wood bribes; beating them pays rewards, and failing to drive them off hurts your plans.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 6.76 from 198 ratings. BGG posters say it makes Caverna tight and punishing like Agricola. Buy it only if you want that harder challenge.
notes: BGG 6.76 over 198 ratings read 2026-10-15. Threads 3025686 and 2956889 (2022-2023): one 2-player group calls it brutal and miserable with abysmally low scores; another poster says it is a deliberate different challenge. A poster also says it is not supposed to be compatible with Forgotten Folk (unverified). The game is text-heavy, with English and German versions only per thread 2978293.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Decrypto base game.
what_it_adds: Category cards that at least one clue each round must match, plus laser and interception tokens that give a second way to win.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.48 from 532 ratings. BGG posters say it gives clue-giving a new angle, but one group dropped it for forcing themed clues. Best for groups that already know Decrypto well.
notes: BGG 7.48 over 532 ratings read 2026-10-15. Threads 2345602 and 2297641 (2019-2020): one poster says it breathed new life into the game; another group binned it after round one. Thread 3596488 asks whether the category cards are language-dependent; no answer was verified.

expansion_name: Five Tribes: The Artisans of Naqala
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Five Tribes base game.
what_it_adds: A sixth tribe of Artisans who craft goods and magic items, workshop and market tiles, a chasm tile and mountain markers that change movement, and two new Djinns.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.12 from 4,313 ratings, the highest of the three. BGG posters name it the first expansion to buy, but posters also report it is out of print and hard to find.
notes: BGG 8.12 over 4313 ratings read 2026-10-15. Threads 1768730 (2017) and 1838782: posters recommend Artisans first; one says it is not a must-have. Thread 2617236 (2021) and 3270792 (2025): posters report no reprint plans, and one quotes a Days of Wonder reply that there are no plans to reprint the expansions (unverified; Days of Wonder site returned 403).

expansion_name: Five Tribes: Whims of the Sultan
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Five Tribes base game.
what_it_adds: Everything needed for five-player games, plus Fabulous Cities and Whims cards that steer your strategy; it can be played with or without Artisans.
what_it_fixes: Lets a fifth person play; the base game seats four.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.95 from 1,810 ratings. BGG posters call the Whims cards good for new players, but those who never play with five see less value and dislike its very high-scoring tiles.
notes: BGG 7.95 over 1810 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 1838782 (2017): one poster picks Whims first because the cards guide new players; others prefer Artisans, citing the five-player part and tiles that can score 125 points.

expansion_name: Five Tribes: The Thieves of Naqala
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Five Tribes base game.
what_it_adds: Six thief cards and one new Djinn: a thief tied to a tribe can make every other player discard resources, tiles or Djinns while you keep something.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.23 from 1,462 ratings, the lowest of the three. BGG posters call it a minor expansion and suggest Artisans first; they add that it suits groups of more than two.
notes: BGG 7.23 over 1462 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 1768730 (2017): posters call it very minor, more interactive and more aggressive.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Forest Shuffle base game.
what_it_adds: 36 multifunctional cards, including two new tree species, that you shuffle into the base deck; some cards add rule twists.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.2 from 3,642 ratings, the highest of the three. It is the expansion used in the online BGA arena play, per a BGG poster, and shuffles straight into the deck.
notes: BGG 8.2 over 3642 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3420077 (2024-2025): a poster plays BGA arena with base + Alpine; others prefer Woodland Edge or both together. Cards are removed based on player count per the publisher description.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Forest Shuffle base game.
what_it_adds: 36 new cards of flora and fauna, including shrubs, that you shuffle into the base deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.1 from 2,744 ratings. BGG posters are split on whether it beats Alpine, but one says the two together create far more combos than either alone.
notes: BGG 8.1 over 2744 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3420077: one poster prefers base + Woodland Edge over base + Alpine; another finds a good chunk of the cards weak; a third prefers both mixed in. A rule thread notes some base cards were retroactively changed.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Forest Shuffle base game.
what_it_adds: A 20-card official solo Automa deck with 12 challenges, five asymmetrical caves replacing the base caves, and 15 rare species cards that were earlier promos.
what_it_fixes: Adds a solo mode; the base game has no official solo play.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.75 from 1,378 ratings. BGG posters say it is mainly for the solo mode, caves and collected promo cards, and one is disappointed it is not much for multiplayer.
notes: BGG 7.75 over 1378 ratings read 2026-10-15. Components come from the BGG publisher description. Threads 3535062 and 3527410 (2025): posters say it is not needed for multiplayer, but is a cheaper way to get the promo cards. One poster quotes $12.99.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: Cleric character card, Resurrect and Bless ability cards, two scorecards and a new 10-card personal deck that replaces the base starting deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.65 from 1,896 ratings. A BGG poster calls the Cleric the most straightforward pack for younger or newer players.
notes: BGG 7.65 over 1,896 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing. Threads 2475263 and 2881037 (2020-2022): posters call character packs the first thing to buy after the base game; one family kept only base + Journeys instead.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: Wizard character card, Channel and Fireball ability cards, two scorecards and a new 10-card personal deck that replaces the base starting deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.66 from 1,903 ratings. One BGG poster says Wizard and Ranger are their favourites.
notes: BGG 7.66 over 1,903 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing. Threads 2475263 and 2881037 (2020-2022): posters call character packs the first thing to buy after the base game; one family kept only base + Journeys instead.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: Ranger character card, Headshot and Track ability cards, two scorecards and a new 10-card personal deck that replaces the base starting deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.67 from 1,871 ratings. One BGG poster says Wizard and Ranger are their favourites.
notes: BGG 7.67 over 1,871 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing. Threads 2475263 and 2881037 (2020-2022): posters call character packs the first thing to buy after the base game; one family kept only base + Journeys instead.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: Fighter character card, Crushing Blow and Shoulder Bash ability cards, two scorecards and a new 10-card personal deck that replaces the base starting deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.68 from 1,859 ratings. It gives a straightforward melee class that swaps in for the base deck.
notes: BGG 7.68 over 1,859 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing. Threads 2475263 and 2881037 (2020-2022): posters call character packs the first thing to buy after the base game; one family kept only base + Journeys instead.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: Thief character card, Heist and Pickpocket ability cards, two scorecards and a new 10-card personal deck that replaces the base starting deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.69 from 1,848 ratings. It gives a steal-focused class that swaps in for the base deck.
notes: BGG 7.69 over 1,848 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing. Threads 2475263 and 2881037 (2020-2022): posters call character packs the first thing to buy after the base game; one family kept only base + Journeys instead.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: 20 Ancestry cards for Dwarf, Elf, Ogre, Orc and Smallfolk that stack on a class for new abilities and items.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.82 from 516 ratings, the best of the small packs. BGG posters say it adds flavour and variety without adding complexity, and mixes with any class.
notes: BGG 7.82 over 516 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing. Threads 2475263, 2498838 and 2466973 (2020-2022) say Ancestry adds flavour without complexity.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: 12 new action and champion cards for the market deck, including Andor the Valiant and Lenka the Hunter.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.67 from 357 ratings. BGG posters call Hunters and Travelers the easiest way to freshen the market, and one family plays base + both.
notes: BGG 7.67 over 357 ratings read 2026-10-15. The Wise Wizard Games store lists the four Journeys packs only as a $19.99 bundle, so no single-pack price is recorded. Threads 2475263, 2466973 and 2881037 (2020-2022) discuss Journeys and quest cards.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: 12 new action and champion cards for the market deck, including Olara the Slayer and Pelleas the Seeker.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.71 from 362 ratings. BGG posters call Hunters and Travelers the easiest way to freshen the market, and one family plays base + both.
notes: BGG 7.71 over 362 ratings read 2026-10-15. The Wise Wizard Games store lists the four Journeys packs only as a $19.99 bundle, so no single-pack price is recorded. Threads 2475263, 2466973 and 2881037 (2020-2022) discuss Journeys and quest cards.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: 12 artifact and quest cards: each quest gives a secret objective and finishing three wins.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.65 from 344 ratings. BGG posters find quests swingy and luck-based in player-versus-player games and not needed solo.
notes: BGG 7.65 over 344 ratings read 2026-10-15. The Wise Wizard Games store lists the four Journeys packs only as a $19.99 bundle, so no single-pack price is recorded. Threads 2475263, 2466973 and 2881037 (2020-2022) discuss Journeys and quest cards.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: 12 artifact and quest cards: each quest gives a secret objective and finishing three wins.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.68 from 333 ratings. BGG posters find quests swingy and luck-based in player-versus-player games and not needed solo.
notes: BGG 7.68 over 333 ratings read 2026-10-15. The Wise Wizard Games store lists the four Journeys packs only as a $19.99 bundle, so no single-pack price is recorded. Threads 2475263, 2466973 and 2881037 (2020-2022) discuss Journeys and quest cards.

expansion_name: Hero Realms: The Ruin of Thandar Campaign Deck
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game and one Character Pack per player.
what_it_adds: Over 140 cards that turn Hero Realms into a cooperative campaign with missions, experience points and treasures added to your starting deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.47 from 2,794 ratings. Pick it only if you want co-op campaign play; it needs a Character Pack per player. Posters call the follow-up campaign short.
notes: BGG 7.47 over 2794 ratings read 2026-10-15; price and the Character Pack requirement from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing.

expansion_name: Hero Realms: The Lost Village Campaign Deck
requires_also: Hero Realms: The Ruin of Thandar Campaign Deck
prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game, The Ruin of Thandar and one Character Pack per player.
what_it_adds: Part two of the Ruin of Thandar campaign: 88 game cards, 12 oversized Master villain cards, 2 challenge cards, a rulebook and an adventure book.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.85 from 704 ratings. A BGG poster says it is cool but short, with three fights. Only worth buying if you enjoyed The Ruin of Thandar.
notes: BGG 7.85 over 704 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing, which showed no variant in stock on 2026-10-15.

expansion_name: Hero Realms: Boss Deck - The Dragon
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: A 30-card Dragon boss deck that replaces a personal deck so one player is the boss against 1-5 hero players.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.58 from 915 ratings. Best with 3-4 players, one BGG poster says, who liked the Dragon more than the Lich.
notes: BGG 7.58 over 915 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing. Threads 2475263 and 2498838 (2020): bosses suit 3-4 players, are poor with two, and are not solo challenges.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Hero Realms base game.
what_it_adds: A 30-card Lich boss deck that replaces a personal deck so one player is the boss against 1-5 hero players.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.64 from 856 ratings. Best with 3-4 players, and one BGG poster calls it a little unbalanced.
notes: BGG 7.64 over 856 ratings read 2026-10-15; price from the Wise Wizard Games Shopify listing. Threads 2475263 and 2498838 (2020): bosses suit 3-4 players, are poor with two, and are not solo challenges.

base_game: Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Robinson Crusoe base game.
what_it_adds: Earlier promos in one box: Gamer and Sailor characters, crewmen, hunting dog, event and mystery cards, shelter upgrades, plus five scenarios including Tracing Doctor Livingstone.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.05 from 701 ratings. BGG posters call it the better first purchase over Mystery Tales: modular add-ins plus revised promos and an interesting Livingstone scenario.
notes: BGG 8.05 over 701 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the Portal Games product page; Portal says the pre-order resin markers are sold separately. Thread 2637985 (2021): one poster says Treasure Chest is a revised edition of earlier promos and a better buy than Mystery Tales; another notes some content such as trait cards goes unused.

base_game: Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Robinson Crusoe base game.
what_it_adds: A five-mission campaign (The Lost City of Z), two standalone scenarios, ten characters, new card decks, and a sanity mechanic that turns the base game into horror.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.86 from 983 ratings. BGG posters call it harder, with about 20 more rule pages, unclear rules and a horror theme shift, and say it suits veterans of the base game.
notes: BGG 7.86 over 983 ratings read 2026-10-15. Description from the BGG publisher text. Threads 2987539 (2022) and 2637985 (2021): several posters report unclear rules and unanswered queries, and one says it is only good for base-game veterans. Portal pledged fixes in later printings (unverified).

base_game: Robinson Crusoe: Adventures on the Cursed Island
expansion_name: Robinson Crusoe: The Book of Adventures
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Robinson Crusoe base game.
what_it_adds: An almanac of 54 new scenarios in the retail edition, ranked by difficulty, complexity and theme, from family-friendly to very hard.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.74 from 493 ratings. Worth it if you have played the base scenarios and want more; the retail book omits eight scenarios found in the Gamefound edition, a BGG poster says.
notes: BGG 7.74 over 493 ratings read 2026-10-15. The retail edition has 54 scenarios and the Gamefound edition (BGG 336650) 60, per the BGG publisher text. The eight-scenario difference is from one poster in thread 3388729 who compared unboxing videos (unverified).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: Four characters (Dark Cultist, Sage, Knight, Merchant), 90 Adventure cards, 26 Spells, 12 Warlock Quest cards and a Grim Reaper figure that players steer against each other.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.34 from 2,848 ratings, the most-rated expansion. A BGG poster always plays with it and says it could be part of the base game; others find it quieter at two players.
notes: BGG 7.34 over 2,848 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 3237456 (2024): one poster always plays with the Reaper and calls it a candidate for base game, one suggests leaving Reaper and Werewolf out at two players, and another says the figure is a small part and the expansion works without it. Thread 2676927 (2021): a poster says any three small boxes including the Reaper. No Amazon listing turned up in US searches on 2026-10-15, so availability is unverified.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: A new Dungeon region board, over 100 new cards and five characters (Gladiator, Amazon, Swashbuckler, Gypsy, Philosopher) with a way to chase a second endgame route.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.34 from 2,214 ratings. BGG posters pick it for a first corner expansion: a risky region with better rewards and a route to the Dungeon Master ending.
notes: BGG 7.34 over 2,214 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 2676927 (2021) and 3237456 (2024): several posters list Dungeon in their top three or call it their favourite corner board. No Amazon listing turned up in US searches on 2026-10-15, so availability is unverified.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: A new Highland region board, over 100 new cards, six characters and the Eagle King; mountain trips pay in gold and gems and add beatable early enemies.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.31 from 1,643 ratings. A BGG poster says it speeds the game up with beatable enemies and plenty of gold, and several list it among their top three expansions.
notes: BGG 7.31 over 1,643 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 2676927 (2021): a poster says the Highland offers more enemies beatable from the start and lots of money. Thread 3237456 (2024): several posters list it in a top three. No Amazon listing turned up in US searches on 2026-10-15, so availability is unverified.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: A City board with its own deck, shops (Stables, Armoury, Magic Emporium), Wanted Poster bounties, new characters and alternative endings.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.44 from 1,317 ratings. A BGG poster calls it a good way to spend gold; another ranks it lowest of the corner boards because it adds shopping rather than adventure.
notes: BGG 7.44 over 1,317 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 2676927 (2021): a poster says City gives more things to do with gold but is not an adventure region. Thread 3237456 (2024): another poster says City is lowest priority if you only want three. Amazon page language reads English (EN).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: A fae-themed Woodland region with five new characters, new alternative endings and the treasures and threats of the Woodland deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.50 from 898 ratings, one of the best-rated corner boards. A BGG poster names it among three adventure regions worth choosing first.
notes: BGG 7.50 over 898 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 2676927 (2021): a poster picks Dungeon, Highland or Woodland as the first big board. Thread 3237456 (2024): another lists Woodland among three. No Amazon listing turned up in US searches on 2026-10-15, so availability is unverified.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: A post-apocalypse board of settlements and mutated nature, with new denizens and cards for a different tone from the fantasy base game.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.62 from 563 ratings, the highest of the large 4th Edition boxes. A BGG poster includes it in their three for the new board and denizens.
notes: BGG 7.62 over 563 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 2676927 (2021): a poster picks Harbinger, Cataclysm, Reaper for new board and denizens. Amazon page language reads English (EN).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: The Harbinger figure and an end-of-the-world timer: demons and plague escalate and everyone loses if no one wins before the world ends.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.27 from 571 ratings. A BGG poster says it adds an end-of-the-world timer so the game cannot drag on, but also makes it harder; another includes it in their top three.
notes: BGG 7.27 over 571 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 2308351 (2019): a poster says it adds an end-of-the-world mechanic where everybody loses if the game runs past a set point, and makes the game harder, while others say no expansion otherwise shortens the game. Thread 3237456 (2024) calls Alliances harder than Harbinger, Dragon and Firelands. Amazon page language reads English (EN).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: Four characters, 84 Adventure cards, 20 Spells, 24 Warlock Quest cards and three alternative endings, including a climactic battle with the Ice Queen.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.15 from 1,660 ratings. A BGG poster says its main gain is more Craft monsters, which the base game lacks; others suggest it or Sacred Pool as general-purpose small boxes.
notes: BGG 7.15 over 1,660 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 2676927 (2021): an owner says it is okay, its main contribution a higher concentration of Craft monsters. Thread 3237456 (2024): a poster suggests Frostmarch or Sacred Pool for more general good stuff. No Amazon listing turned up in US searches on 2026-10-15, so availability is unverified.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: Four characters (Chivalric Knight, Dread Knight, Cleric, Magus), alternative endings, Stable cards, Quest Reward cards and Neutral alignment cards.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.22 from 1,391 ratings. A BGG poster pairs it with the Reaper as one pick and another suggests it for general good cards; it is a variety pack with no new region.
notes: BGG 7.22 over 1,391 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 3237456 (2024): one poster counts Reaper plus Sacred Pool as one pick, another suggests Frostmarch or Sacred Pool for more general good stuff. Amazon listing language was checked as English (EN) on the City and Cataclysm pages only.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: Over 100 Adventure cards, new spells, characters and endings, plus a Day/Night Time card that flips on Events and a roaming Werewolf.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.28 from 1,175 ratings. A BGG poster lists it among the three to pick, but another suggests leaving the Werewolf out at two players, where landing on an opponent is rare.
notes: BGG 7.28 over 1,175 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 3237456 (2024): one poster names Werewolf / Blood Moon among three picks, another suggests leaving out Reaper and Werewolf at two players.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: The Ifrit and a fire that burns away resources and sets whole regions ablaze; players race for the Crown of Command before it spreads.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.08 from 649 ratings, the lowest of the 4th Edition small boxes except Dragon. A BGG poster calls Alliances harder than Firelands, Harbinger and Dragon, so it adds real pressure.
notes: BGG 7.08 over 649 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 3376319 (2024): a 4th Edition player lists Harbinger, Dragons and Firelands as the harder expansions.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: The Nether Realm and The Deep Realms reissued as one set: Nether Deck enemies such as the Pyrochanter and Titan Wraith, plus the Deep Realms content.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.23 from only 154 ratings. It reissues two older small boxes in one set; buy it only if you want both, since the Nether Realm and Deep Realms are not listed in this guide.
notes: BGG 7.23 over 154 ratings read 2026-10-15. Description from the BGG publisher text: it combines The Nether Realm (BGG 152319, 7.09, 353 ratings) and The Deep Realms (BGG 169254, 7.13, 272 ratings). Those two are not listed separately because the 2018 set contains both. No Amazon listing turned up in US searches on 2026-10-15, so availability is unverified.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman Revised 4th Edition base game.
what_it_adds: A dual-sided Inner Region (familiar terrain or the Dragon Tower), six characters, over 300 tokens and cards, and Draconic Lords that grow stronger over the game.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 6.89 from 1,274 ratings, the lowest of the 4th Edition expansions. A BGG owner sold it for adding complication to a light game; Alliances is called harder than Dragon.
notes: BGG 6.89 over 1,274 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 2676927 (2021): one owner sold it as the only expansion he regrets, saying it adds unnecessary complication to a beer-and-pretzels game. Thread 3376319 (2024): a poster lists Dragons among the harder expansions.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman 5th Edition base game, a separate box from the Revised 4th Edition.
what_it_adds: A cooperative campaign of five Trials with a Doom Tracker; heroes place Talismans on Places of Power, unseal a Portal and beat each Trial's adversary, unlocking sealed boxes of cards.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.35 from 148 ratings. Co-op only and campaign-based, with a high difficulty a BGG group lost three games at three players; buy it for co-op, not for variety in normal play.
notes: BGG 7.35 over 148 ratings read 2026-10-15. Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 3335873 (2024): posters say the cards are scenario-specific and mostly unusable in a normal game. Thread 3376319 (2024): one group lost three games in a row at three players; another beat the trials after losing the first two.

expansion_name: Talisman: Nemesis - Call of the Hunt
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman 5th Edition base game, a separate box from the Revised 4th Edition.
what_it_adds: One-versus-many play: heroes cooperate through three Trials with unique adversaries and villains while one Nemesis player commands beasts; opening boxes unlocks new cards and figures.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.77 from only 41 ratings. It needs at least three players and one of them plays the Nemesis, so it suits groups that want a one-vs-many mode, not the standard race.
notes: BGG 7.77 over 41 ratings read 2026-10-15 (BGG lists 3-6 players). Contents from the BGG publisher text. Thread 3611254 (2025) title says the action cards make it too easy for the Nemesis player to win (thread not read in full).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Talisman 5th Edition base game, a separate box from the Revised 4th Edition.
what_it_adds: Gothic-horror Dracula theme: play Mina Harker or Van Helsing, race to Dracula's Castle overlay, with new enemies, events, magical objects and Ongoing Event cards.
notes: Not ranked: BGG lists 2026 with 8 ratings (9.12) and no reviews, so there is not enough evidence for a verdict. Contents from the BGG publisher text; the Amazon title says it requires Talisman 5th Edition.

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve more ships and bases for the trade deck, with new high-cost cards and base synergies, more of the same while making games more epic.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.69 from 2,354 ratings. The Geeks Under Grace guide calls Crisis ships and bases the most basic expansions and the first to buy after the core set; it leans to this pack for Star Empire.
notes: BGG 7.69 over 2,354 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 5.99 and in-stock status from the Wise Wizard Shopify listing. A BGG poster says one pack is enough for a two-player game; thread 3237569 suggests playing Crisis packs with the original core set. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve more ships and bases for the trade deck, giving each faction cheaper cards plus 5-8 cost ones for bigger turns.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.68 from 2,143 ratings. The guide groups it with Bases & Battleships as the simplest more-of-the-same pack and says it hardly matters which you buy first.
notes: BGG 7.68 over 2,143 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 5.99 and in-stock status from the Wise Wizard Shopify listing (product handle reads copy-of-crisis-bases-battleships-1). Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Gambit cards: two face-down per player that you reveal and scrap at any time for extra trade, damage or draws; these gambits are crazier than the first set.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.23 from 981 ratings. The guide calls Cosmic Gambit the better deal for testing Gambits: cheaper than the Gambit Set, though it has no solo or co-op cards.
notes: BGG 7.23 over 981 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 6.99 from the Wise Wizard listing. The guide suggests dealing three Gambits and choosing two, since some are better than others. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

expansion_name: Star Realms: Command Deck - The Alliance
prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: A Commander character with a higher authority total, a unique starting deck, two unique Gambits and a multicolor 8-cost ship that enters the trade deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.63 from 414 ratings. The guide says Command Decks are awesome, that a fair duel needs two, and suggests starting with Alliance (blue and yellow) and Union.
notes: BGG 7.63 over 414 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 6.99 from the Wise Wizard listing. The guide names Nandi (The Alliance, blue/yellow) its favourite Commander. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

expansion_name: Star Realms: Command Deck - The Union
prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: A Commander character with a higher authority total, a unique starting deck, two unique Gambits and a multicolor 8-cost ship that enters the trade deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.61 from 390 ratings. The guide suggests Union (green and yellow) paired with Alliance as the two Commanders to start with, since the Legends finals used both.
notes: BGG 7.61 over 390 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 6.99 from the Wise Wizard listing. The guide describes Alliance versus Union as tricky versus aggressive play. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve ships and bases built around Double Ally abilities, with no new mechanic beyond that.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.75 from 182 ratings. The guide calls it a good early pack, especially if you started with Frontiers, though veterans may find it unexciting.
notes: BGG 7.75 over 182 ratings read 2026-10-15. The $5.99 per-pack MSRP is stated in the guide; the Wise Wizard shop sells High Alert as a $19.99 four-pack bundle of 48 cards. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve ships and bases that cost one less for each card of the same faction you have in play, producing fast games.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.71 from 179 ratings. The guide says the discount mechanic with strong Blob and Star Empire cards gives very fast games and is another good early pack.
notes: BGG 7.71 over 179 ratings read 2026-10-15. Per-pack MSRP from the guide; sold as a four-pack bundle by Wise Wizard. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve dual-faction ships and bases that trigger ally bonuses for either of their two factions.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.78 from 657 ratings. The guide says dual-faction cards are generally a little weaker but more flexible; buy Crisis ships and bases first so they do not dazzle you.
notes: BGG 7.78 over 657 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 5.99 from the Wise Wizard listing. Wise Wizard also sells a $19.99 United bundle. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve dual-faction ships and bases that trigger ally bonuses for either faction, with a high density of expensive bases.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.75 from 642 ratings. The guide groups it with Assault as more dual-faction ships and bases, best bought after the Crisis ships-and-bases packs.
notes: BGG 7.75 over 642 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 5.99 from the Wise Wizard listing. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: The first Hero cards: low-cost cards that go straight into play, cannot be attacked, and are scrapped for a bonus plus a faction ally trigger.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.03 from 2,240 ratings. BGG's lowest-rated Crisis pack. The guide says Heroes change the game and recommends this simpler pack before United Heroes.
notes: BGG 7.03 over 2,240 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 5.99 from the Wise Wizard listing (product handle reads copy-of-crisis-bases-battleships-2). Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

expansion_name: Star Realms: Command Deck - The Pact
prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: A Commander character with a higher authority total, a unique starting deck, two unique Gambits and a multicolor 8-cost ship that enters the trade deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.65 from 395 ratings. The guide says to buy all the Command Decks eventually, starting with Alliance and Union; this one is a fair pairing for a duel.
notes: BGG 7.65 over 395 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 6.99 from the Wise Wizard listing.  Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: A Commander character with a higher authority total, a unique starting deck, two unique Gambits and a multicolor 8-cost ship that enters the trade deck.
