notes: BGG 7.55 over 422 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 6.99 from the Wise Wizard listing.  Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Gambit cards plus solo and co-op cards and three Merc Cruisers for the trade deck.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.21 from 2,306 ratings. The guide likes Gambits but says Cosmic Gambit is the better first buy; this set adds solo and co-op cards and may feel underwhelming second.
notes: BGG 7.21 over 2,306 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 9.99 from the Wise Wizard listing. Contents (solo and co-op cards, three Merc Cruisers) from the guide. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve Mission cards dealt three per player; completing one pays a reward, and flipping your third mission wins the game.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.29 from 621 ratings. The guide says Missions turn Star Realms into a different game and are challenging, though it took time to warm to them; app players are split.
notes: BGG 7.29 over 621 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 5.99 from the Wise Wizard listing. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Event cards shuffled into the trade deck that resolve when revealed, such as clearing the row, dealing damage or giving authority.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.13 from 2,281 ratings. The guide says Events amplify randomness and make games swingier, which it enjoys; it calls them one of the most controversial packs among app players.
notes: BGG 7.13 over 2,281 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 5.99 from the Wise Wizard listing (product handle reads copy-of-crisis-bases-battleships). Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve Hero cards costing 3-5 trade that give a bonus when bought and another when scrapped.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.29 from 641 ratings. The guide likes them but notes the rules are confusing and Heroes are not automatic buys; start with the simpler Crisis Heroes first.
notes: BGG 7.29 over 641 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 5.99 from the Wise Wizard listing. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve cards including Tech cards that grant abilities you can activate each turn by paying trade.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.42 from 185 ratings. The guide says Tech is pricey and takes many games to appreciate, so get it once you are experienced.
notes: BGG 7.42 over 185 ratings read 2026-10-15. Per-pack MSRP from the guide; sold as a four-pack bundle by Wise Wizard. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twelve multi-faction Hero cards with a comes-into-play line like United but dual faction symbols.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.33 from 177 ratings. The guide calls it fairly underwhelming and the most complicated to understand; a BGG poster calls it the best set, so taste varies.
notes: BGG 7.33 over 177 ratings read 2026-10-15. Per-pack MSRP from the guide; sold as a four-pack bundle by Wise Wizard. Thread 3676973 (2026): a poster calls High Alert: Heroes the best set ever made while admitting bias. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Twenty Scenario cards; one is flipped at the start of a game and permanently changes the rules for it.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.63 from 502 ratings. The guide says the app's weekly Arena covers the same idea, so it is no priority unless you avoid digital play. Listed out of stock at Wise Wizard.
notes: BGG 7.63 over 502 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 7.99 and out-of-stock flag from the Wise Wizard Shopify listing on 2026-10-15. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs a Star Realms core set; add one copy of each expansion to the shared trade deck.
what_it_adds: Fifteen alternate-art promo cards including Battle Barge, Fortress Oblivion and The Ark, with errata applied.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.75 from 538 ratings. The guide says save it for later; The Ark is among the most complained-about cards. Buy it for the Kickstarter promo cards only. Out of stock at Wise Wizard.
notes: BGG 7.75 over 538 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 9.99 and out-of-stock flag from the Wise Wizard Shopify listing on 2026-10-15; contents list from that listing. Opinion from the Geeks Under Grace Complete Star Realms Buyer's Guide (page read 2026-10-15).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Istanbul base game.
what_it_adds: Four new places to visit, more interaction between players, a coffee good and new ways to earn rubies via the tavern and guild hall.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.88 from 3,415 ratings. A BGG poster says that if you buy only one Istanbul expansion, buy this; others call both expansions good but not necessary.
notes: BGG 7.88 over 3,415 ratings read 2026-10-15. Description from the BGG publisher text. Thread 2929629 (2022): a poster says to get Mocha & Baksheesh if you only get one; another notes it and Letters & Seals were still sold by several shops. Thread 2065351 (2018): several owners say the base game is great alone and the expansions are nice but not necessary. Posters also mention a Big Box with base and both expansions (unverified).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Istanbul base game.
what_it_adds: Mail delivery to shopkeepers for money, secret-society information sold for rubies, and a slower companion who needs no assistants.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.73 from 1,633 ratings. Buy it second: a BGG poster says to get Mocha & Baksheesh first, and several owners call both expansions fun spice rather than necessary.
notes: BGG 7.73 over 1,633 ratings read 2026-10-15. Description from the BGG publisher text. Threads 2929629 (2022) and 2065351 (2018): posters rank Mocha & Baksheesh first and call the expansions optional add-ons.

expansion_name: Star Wars: Rebellion - Rise of the Empire
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Star Wars: Rebellion base game.
what_it_adds: Eight new leaders, 36 miniatures, new missions, three new dice and tactic cards that make combat more cinematic, themed on Rogue One.
what_it_fixes: Replaces the luck-heavy base combat cards with a tactic-card system that rewards planning, according to many owners.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.87 from 5,412 ratings. Many owners say they would not play without it because of the better combat and added variety; a few prefer the base combat.
notes: BGG 8.87 over 5,412 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3672813 (2026): owners say it turns an 8/10 into a 10/10, and that its combat replaces rather than adds to the base combat. Thread 3185911 (2023): one poster says the base game is fine alone if you do not care about Rogue One, and another says some players never wanted the new combat. Thread 3606817 (2025): a poster advises learning the base game first. The FFG page lists the Rise of the Empire rulebook; it has no store button.

expansion_name: Too Many Bones: 40 Days in Daelore
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: 40 new encounters and 15 new Baddies, with General, Special, Solo and Tyrant encounters, for land-based adventures in the base game or Undertow.
verdict_reason: Most-rated content pack at 8.77 from 1,163 ratings. It adds 40 encounters and 15 Baddies to the base game at the same price as a Gearloc box; owners often pair it with Age of Tyranny.
notes: BGG 8.77 over 1,163 ratings read 2026-10-15. Chip Theory page: compatible with the base game and Undertow, focused on land-based encounters that expand Goblins, Bogs, Scales, Beasts, Trolls and Orcs. Thread 3516784 (2025): one owner had it on the way as the first add-on.

expansion_name: Too Many Bones: The Age of Tyranny
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: Campaign mode with a Snapshot Mat, Scars and Boons, plus 21 new Day 1-3 encounters that add early-game variety even if you never play the campaign.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.57 from 1,070 ratings. Chip Theory calls its 21 early encounters essential for veterans; BGG posters call them nice variety but not essential if you skip the campaign.
notes: BGG 8.57 over 1,070 ratings read 2026-10-15. Publisher page: the Day 1-3 encounters are "considered one of the most essential add-ons" by veteran players (publisher claim). Thread 3516784 (2025): one poster would not buy it without interest in campaign mode; another buys it for the encounters and calls them nice-to-have.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A scout Gearloc with traps and animal companions who works solo or in a party, with a character mat, chip, skill dice, stat dice and initiative die.
verdict_reason: Most-rated Gearloc at 8.76 from 1,462 ratings. A BGG player loves his traps and pets but warns he can end Tyrant fights too easily if you want a hard game.
notes: BGG 8.76 over 1,462 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3652256 (2026-01): a poster loves Ghillie but suggests skipping him to avoid easy Tyrant endings.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A steambot Gearloc with modes to blitz, blast, ram and scram, whose skills stay available for longer.
verdict_reason: Highest rating of the original Gearlocs at 8.78 from 1,009 ratings. A BGG player names Gasket and Stanza as favourites for their prolonged access to skills.
notes: BGG 8.78 over 1,009 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3652256 (2026-01): a poster says Gasket and Stanza let you keep skills available longer and are two of his favourites.

expansion_name: Too Many Bones: Nugget (The Treasure Hunter)
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A treasure-hunting Gearloc who can switch between melee and ranged attacks, with the usual Gearloc mat, chip, skill dice, stat dice and initiative die.
verdict_reason: BGG rates her 8.72 from 1,272 ratings. Chip Theory sells her as a versatile choice because she can switch between melee and ranged attacks.
notes: BGG 8.72 over 1,272 ratings read 2026-10-15. Versatility comes from the Chip Theory description. A 2025 BGG poster listed Nugget among the Gearlocs they already owned.

expansion_name: Too Many Bones: Rage of Tyranny
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or Undertow.
what_it_adds: Alternate, harder versions of 12 Tyrants for the base game and Undertow, with persistent effects during the adventure plus nasty Loot cards.
what_it_fixes: Makes Tyrant fights harder for groups that find the base game too easy.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.71 from 212 ratings. Owners buy it for harder Tyrants, so it suits groups that already beat the base game; one owner admits to not playing it much.
notes: BGG 8.71 over 212 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3516784 (2025): one owner says Rage is mainly for raising boss difficulty and rarely plays it; threads 3652256 and 3602614 describe it as a way to even up large parties.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A geologist Gearloc who slings iron, nickel and cobalt orbs around the battlefield, with the usual Gearloc mat, chip and dice.
verdict_reason: BGG rates her 8.69 from 251 ratings. Choose her if you like an orb-slinging ranged Gearloc; there is little community comparison beyond the rating.
notes: BGG 8.69 over 251 ratings read 2026-10-15. Little BGG discussion found; one forum buyer listed Polaris as a planned purchase (thread 3602614).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A martial-arts brawler Gearloc who is a one-stop melee fighter, with meditation-fuelled skills for solo and party play.
verdict_reason: BGG rates him 8.66 from 261 ratings. Choose him if you want a melee Gearloc; community discussion is thin beyond the rating.
notes: BGG 8.66 over 261 ratings read 2026-10-15. Little BGG discussion found; one forum buyer listed Static as a planned purchase (thread 3602614).

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A half-boar, half-Gearloc ranged fighter with a dual-sided mat, apothecary tools and darts, with the usual Gearloc dice.
verdict_reason: BGG rates her 8.47 from 504 ratings. A BGG poster picks Dart, Carcass and Riffle as the Gearlocs with the highest skill ceiling, so she suits players who like a challenge.
notes: BGG 8.47 over 504 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3714519 (2026-05): a poster recommends Dart, Carcass and Riffle for the most demanding Gearlocs; another BGG user calls Dart a favourite.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: An ex-chef Gearloc who hunts with meat hooks and cooks recipes that buff and heal the party.
verdict_reason: BGG rates him 8.73 from 251 ratings. Owners disagree: some call him a favourite and a must-have, others find him fiddly, so check his sheet on the Chip Theory site first.
notes: BGG 8.73 over 251 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3693962 (2026-04): opinions range from favourite Gearloc to disappointing; one player says he needs different tactics in early, mid and late game.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A Gearloc who plays much more like a card-driven deck builder than the other Gearlocs.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.68 from 377 ratings. Posters call Riffle fun and powerful but very different from other Gearlocs, so it suits fans of deck building.
notes: BGG 8.68 over 377 ratings read 2026-10-15. Not listed on the Chip Theory store when checked, so no store link and no price. Thread 3602614 (2025-10): posters describe Riffle as very different and a good fit for deck-builder fans.

expansion_name: Too Many Bones: Tink (The Bot Builder)
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: An old Gearloc who builds and accessorises Spiderbots to disable Baddie skills, protect allies or attack.
verdict_reason: BGG rates him 8.54 from 964 ratings. One owner calls Tink a challenge pick, so he suits players who want a harder, more fiddly Gearloc.
notes: BGG 8.54 over 964 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3602614 (2025-10) and thread 3693962 (2026-04): an owner calls him a challenge choice.

expansion_name: Too Many Bones: Lab Rats (The Escapists)
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: Four Gearlocs in one box with four character mats and chips and a new way of combining skill dice.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.49 from 421 ratings. A BGG poster calls the Lab Rats unusual with fewer build options than other Gearlocs, so they suit players who want a tag-team novelty.
notes: BGG 8.49 over 421 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 3714519 (2026-05): a poster says Lab Rats are unique and unusual but do not have many build options.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: Five new Tyrants, 30 dual-type Baddies and a Build-a-Tyrant mode that stress-tests your Gearlocs.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.43 from 585 ratings. It is designed to be hard, but it is out of stock at Chip Theory with no reprint date, so you may only find it second hand.
notes: BGG 8.43 over 585 ratings read 2026-10-15. Out of stock at the Chip Theory store on 2026-10-15. Thread 3706563 (2026-05): a poster says a reprint is planned but with no date. Thread 3516784: a poster is not a big fan of it.

expansion_name: Too Many Bones: The Automaton of Shale
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A pop-up book containing a one-off Too Many Bones adventure with new encounters, Baddies and Loot that you can also mix into existing content.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.68 from 266 ratings. Chip Theory calls it a novelty pop-up adventure; buy it as a collector piece, because the extra encounters are a bonus.
notes: BGG 8.68 over 266 ratings read 2026-10-15. Publisher says it can be played front to back as one session or mixed into existing content; the Gameplay Pack is a separate item at 17.95.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Too Many Bones base game or a standalone box such as Undertow.
what_it_adds: A kobold Gearloc with few skill dice of his own who converts your existing dice faces into new effects and reuses them via a Heatup Track.
verdict_reason: BGG rates him 8.49 from only 37 ratings, because he is new in 2026. A forum owner bought him alongside Carcass and Rage of Tyranny; evidence is thin.
notes: BGG 8.49 over 37 ratings read 2026-10-15. Released on the Chip Theory store 2026-04-01. Thread 3693962 (2026-04): an owner says Trover brought him back to buying more TMB content.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Tapestry base game.
what_it_adds: A fifth advancement track with a new card type, income-track upgrades, new capital city mats, revised civilizations and extra tapestry, tech and landmark cards.
what_it_fixes: Opens up the tight four-track board in four- and five-player games, according to BGG players.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.38 from 1,576 ratings. It is the only expansion that changes play: its fifth track relieves four- and five-player crowding, though two posters prefer the simpler base game.
notes: BGG 8.38 over 1,576 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 45.00 (compare-at 50.00) from the Stonemaier Shopify listing. Thread 3524803 (2025): one poster would add it first because the fifth track opens the game up; another says his groups only liked four- and five-player games once the track was added; one group plays with everything except the fifth track.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Tapestry base game.
what_it_adds: Individual landmark goals, revised civilizations, new tapestry cards, new space tiles, a pre-game step so everyone can claim a landmark, and four Automa cards.
what_it_fixes: Landmark drafting in reverse turn order softens the first-player advantage, according to a BGG player.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.11 from 2,333 ratings, the most rated expansion. It adds variety and personal landmark goals without changing the rules much, and BGG posters say add it once you want more.
notes: BGG 8.11 over 2,333 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 32.00 (compare-at 40.00). Thread 3524803: it is mainly more stuff plus one pre-game step; thread 3343894 (2024): a poster adds landmark cards after the first play to blunt the first-player edge.

expansion_name: Tapestry: Revised, Adjusted, Rebalanced Civilization Pack
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Tapestry base game; only useful for printings without revised civs.
what_it_adds: 31 revised civilization mats and 2 capital city mats from the base game and first two expansions, a landmark guide and complexity ratings for every civilization.
what_it_fixes: Rebalances civilizations and adds complexity ratings, so uneven civ strength matters less.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.49 from 206 ratings. Skip it if your base box has the revised-civs banner, since newer printings include those civs; owners of older boxes need it only after many plays.
notes: Not in the ranking row; added because it fixes the balance problems BGG discussions focus on. Thread 3393260 (2024): the designer says the latest printing includes the revised civs and the pack is for older copies. Thread 3778043 (2026): a poster says the game is fine without the changes unless you play enough to notice small power differences.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Tapestry base game.
what_it_adds: Ten fantasy and sci-fi civilizations, six advanced capital city mats, 38 tapestry cards, 12 tech cards, one-time charm effects and a combined rulebook for the base game and all expansions.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.30 from 868 ratings. It adds odd twists on familiar rules, and BGG posters say to wait until everyone knows the game; the combined rulebook helps with the other expansions.
notes: BGG 8.30 over 868 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 22.00 (compare-at 25.00). Threads 3524803 and 3343894: posters leave it out of first plays because of its mechanic twists.

expansion_name: Raiders of the North Sea: Hall of Heroes
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Raiders of the North Sea base game.
what_it_adds: A mead hall board, large player boards, mead to boost crews, quests, reputation and new townsfolk, plus components for a fifth player.
what_it_fixes: Reduces randomness and gives spare hand cards a use through quests, according to BGG players.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.21 from 3,617 ratings. BGG threads name it the usual first expansion; one player finds it drags at two players, and Garphill lists it out of stock.
notes: BGG 8.21 over 3,617 ratings read 2026-10-15. The Garphill Shopify listing was out of stock on 2026-10-15 (price 35.00); other retailers may still have it. Thread 2294834 (2019): most posters name it the best first expansion. Thread 2560629 (2020): one player finds it needs more players and drags at two.

expansion_name: Raiders of the North Sea: Fields of Fame
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Raiders of the North Sea base game.
what_it_adds: A township board, enemy jarl tokens and cards, fame and damage tracking with blood counters, and new townsfolk, plus components for a fifth player.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.02 from 2,901 ratings. Many players use both expansions; one calls the Jarl rules a slowdown, while others prefer it at two players and like the lasting raid consequences.
notes: BGG 8.02 over 2,901 ratings read 2026-10-15. Price 35.00 from the Garphill Shopify listing, in stock. Thread 2560629 (2020): opinions split, one player skips it for the Jarl rules, another prefers it at two players. Thread 2416249 (2020): a poster notes the Jarl tokens are smaller than the others.

expansion_name: Raiders of the North Sea: The North Sea Runesaga
prerequisite_rule: Needs Raiders of the North Sea plus Shipwrights and Explorers of the North Sea.
what_it_adds: A saga competition across all three North Sea games, where first-to-achieve objectives award Runestones and advantages in later chapters, with a Chieftain title for the winner.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.24 from 385 ratings, well below the other expansions. It only works if you own all three North Sea games, so buy it only for a trilogy campaign.
notes: BGG 7.24 over 385 ratings read 2026-10-15. Garphill description: players progress through the Shipwrights, Raiders and Explorers chapters; price 30.00 and in stock. Ranking row flags that it requires the original trilogy.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Space Base base game.
what_it_adds: A large pool of new cards with extra paths to victory for experienced players and only a few simple new rules for newer players.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.42 from 238 ratings. BGG posters who dislike the saga expansions single it out as the one that adds variety with little overhead and does not need the other expansions.
notes: BGG 8.42 over 238 ratings read 2026-10-15. Threads 3192837 and 3102007 (2023, before release): posters say it looks like the expansion for people who want variety without more rules, and that it does not require the other expansions. The AEG product page lists it with a Buy Now button, but the AEG store page for it returned Not Found on 2026-10-15, so no price or store link is given.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Space Base base game.
what_it_adds: Hypernet colony cards that can be placed in any sector instead of an assigned one, giving more variety to the late game.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.08 from 199 ratings. Several BGG posters name it their favourite mini expansion; it adds colony-card variety without adding complexity, and costs $9.99 at AEG.
notes: BGG 8.08 over 199 ratings read 2026-10-15. AEG store page 9.99, InStock on 2026-10-15. Threads 2968464 and 3192837: posters call Biodome the better addition and say it adds little complexity.

expansion_name: Space Base: The Emergence of Shy Pluto
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Space Base base game.
what_it_adds: Story-based scenarios that introduce new ships and modules one by one, which you can then mix permanently into the core game.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.69 from 1,556 ratings. BGG players split: some say it is the only expansion that improves the game, while others find its cards overpowered or dislike the ship tokens and dice.
notes: BGG 7.69 over 1,556 ratings read 2026-10-15. AEG store page 34.99 and OutOfStock on 2026-10-15. Thread 3192837: one poster says only this one enhances the base game; thread 2968464: one says its cards are overpowered; thread 3102007: one dislikes the ship tokens and pink and red dice.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Space Base base game.
what_it_adds: Two new Commodore captains and two new zones, with extra dice and components that raise the player count to seven.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.74 from 886 ratings. A BGG poster calls it a great addition for larger groups, but AEG sells it for $44.99, about the base game price, so it suits groups of five or more.
notes: BGG 7.74 over 886 ratings read 2026-10-15, 2 to 7 players. AEG store page 44.99, InStock on 2026-10-15. Thread 2968464: a poster says it is a great addition for a larger group; thread 3102007: another bought it on a sale for about half price.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the Space Base base game.
what_it_adds: Twelve level-2 ships, many with multiple rewards or Hard Way rewards for rolling doubles.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.78 from 235 ratings. Owners call it twelve more cards of the same game; some like the variety, one thinks it was a waste of money if you buy the bigger expansions.
notes: BGG 7.78 over 235 ratings read 2026-10-15. AEG store page 9.99, InStock on 2026-10-15. Threads 3192837 and 2968464: owners say it does not change the game but adds variety; one says it may be worth having only if you do not buy the bigger expansions.

expansion_name: Space Base: The Mysteries of Terra Proxima
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Space Base base game.
what_it_adds: A second saga with new ruins and fungi-themed cards and a new way to expand the game, intended for players with many plays.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.53 from 299 ratings, the lowest of the set. Posters warn it can unbalance play when combined with Shy Pluto, so buy it only after many plays of the base game.
notes: BGG 7.53 over 299 ratings read 2026-10-15. AEG store page 34.99, InStock on 2026-10-15. Thread 3102007 (2023): one player says it becomes unbalanced and unplayable with both sagas; another does not plan to add it. Thread 2968464: a poster only recommends it after a lot of plays.

prerequisite_rule: Needs the regular Takenoko base game; BGG posters say the tiles do not fit the Collector's Edition.
what_it_adds: A female panda miniature giving an extra action, nine baby-panda tiles, six plot tiles with sacred hills and a Kami garden, an extra pond, 18 cards and 17 bamboo pieces.
what_it_fixes: Lets you swap objectives and use the Gardener spot to reduce luck from the card draw, according to BGG owners.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.52 from 4,609 ratings, above the base game. Several BGG owners say it cuts the luck of the base game, and one would have traded the base game away without it.
notes: BGG 7.52 over 4,609 ratings read 2026-10-15 against 7.20 for the base game. Thread 1983755 (2018): owners say the Gardener cabin tile and Miss Panda's objective swap reduce luck. Thread 1957668 (2018): owners say it adds enough strategy for adults and is still family friendly. Thread 1506877 (2016): posters say the regular Chibis tiles are smaller than, and do not work with, the Collector's Edition. The Bombyx US rulebook link is a PDF and was not opened, so no publisher store link is given.

expansion_name: It's a Wonderful World: Corruption & Ascension
prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game (It's a Wonderful World); the Ascension cards are shuffled in or left out as you choose.
what_it_adds: A separate deck of Ascension cards with corruption cards, pair scoring and bigger point values, plus an extra Oceania empire card and components for more players.
what_it_fixes: Gives a higher scoring ceiling and a corruption trade-off that BGG owners say makes games more varied.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.12 from 2,111 ratings, above the base game. BGG owners recommend it and say they will not play without it.
notes: BGG 8.12 over 2,111 ratings read 2026-10-15 against 7.62 for the base game. Thread 2882466 (2022): owners prefer to play with it and note corruption choices and multipliers; thread 2538332 (2020): review lists new card types. BGG lists 1-7 players; some retailers list 6 and thread 2538332 says the box claims 7, so the top player count is unverified. The publisher store lists the English KSE version with 56 cards, 2 Empire cards and a score board; no price was shown to a plain fetch.

expansion_name: It's a Wonderful World: Leisure & Decadence
prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game (It's a Wonderful World); BGG owners say only one of its two booster packs can be used at a time.
what_it_adds: A campaign of six scenarios with envelopes and secret boxes, plus Culture and Celebrities and Workers modules you can keep using in normal games.
what_it_fixes: Adds scripted scenarios and persistent modules for groups that like campaign play.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.02 from only 366 ratings. Owners disagree: some say the unlocked modules add real depth, others say it is only for campaign fans.
notes: BGG 8.02 over 366 ratings read 2026-10-15. Thread 2430424 (2020): one poster says you miss nothing unless you like campaigns, another says the campaign unlocks two permanent modules (Culture & Celebrities and Workers). Thread 2359670 (2020): posters note only one of the two Leisure & Decadence booster packs can be added at a time. Publisher store lists it as 'Leisure and Decadence (KS01 campaign) EN' with 150 cards, 11 leaflets, 6 envelopes and 4 secret boxes; no price shown to a plain fetch. It is one-time reveal content, not a classic legacy game.

expansion_name: It's a Wonderful World: War or Peace
prerequisite_rule: Needs the base game (It's a Wonderful World); the publisher sells it inside the Heritage box with the base game.
what_it_adds: A five-scenario campaign in envelopes where your choices tip the story towards peace or world war, with extra cards and rewards carried between games.
what_it_fixes: Adds scripted scenarios with story and carry-over rewards to a game otherwise played as repeated score chases.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 7.73 from 1,267 ratings, slightly above the base game. It suits groups who want a campaign, and the publisher sells it only inside the Heritage box.
notes: BGG 7.73 over 1,267 ratings read 2026-10-15 against 7.62 for the base game. The only publisher store product found that contains it is the English Heritage version (Kickstarter), which lists the core game, the Stretch Goals, War or Peace and Leisure and Decadence; no price shown to a plain fetch. Whether War or Peace is also sold alone at retailers is unverified.

base_game: The Lord of the Rings: Journeys in Middle-earth
expansion_name: The Lord of the Rings: Journeys in Middle-earth: Shadowed Paths
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Journeys in Middle-earth base game and the free companion app.
what_it_adds: A new 13-scenario campaign through Mirkwood and Moria, plus new heroes, enemies, terrain and items that also work in other adventures.
what_it_fixes: Adds the campaign and hero variety that BGG owners say the base game lacks.
verdict_reason: BGG rates it 8.60 from 2,189 ratings. An owner review says the base game has only two campaigns and few heroes, which this expansion addresses.
notes: BGG 8.60 over 2,189 ratings read 2026-10-15 against 7.89 for the base game. Thread 2486725 (2020): reviewer says base game replay value is limited by two campaigns and few heroes; another owner notes its new cards are cut slightly wider than first-printing base cards, so sleeves are needed. No per-product Fantasy Flight Games store page was verified; the product-line page was linked instead.

base_game: The Lord of the Rings: Journeys in Middle-earth
expansion_name: The Lord of the Rings: Journeys in Middle-earth: Spreading War
prerequisite_rule: Needs the Journeys in Middle-earth base game and the free companion app.
what_it_adds: A 15-scenario campaign across Rohan and Gondor, with six new heroes, 21 enemy miniatures, 18 double-sided map tiles, new roles and terrain.
what_it_fixes: Adds the largest campaign plus map tiles and heroes, and extra variety that owners say the base game lacks.
